A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoElicit research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and figures, tables, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original elicitation experiments, cross-agent transfer results, human annotation, reproducibility testing, and vulnerability meta-analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds model evaluations, competing-method comparisons, component ablations, and an annotation study of evaluator-negative trajectories.

M1.justification: The proposed seed-generation stage, nested execution and quality refinement loops, and prompt templates remain unchanged. The Operator-specific summarizer model and component-removal experiments introduce experimental configurations, rather than a revised AutoElicit algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OSWorld OS and Multi-Apps coverage, including 361 seeds spanning 66 tasks and 117 transfer instructions. Added experiments vary models, subsets, and controls without introducing another task domain or environment.

E2.justification: v1 discusses TAI3 as related work but does not evaluate competing elicitation pipelines. v2 Appendix K.1 adds TAI3-Adapted and SelfRef as evaluated baselines, comparing elicitation success, severity, and perturbation quality in Tables 12–13.

E3.justification: v2 adds a random 120-seed Opus 4.5 evaluation alongside the retained high-severity subsets, full-pipeline Operator evaluation with GPT-5.4-mini summarization, and high-severity Opus 4.6 testing. New protocols include baseline execution budgets, 48 seed-generation configurations with diversity metrics, and human review of 50 evaluator-negative trajectories.

E4.justification: New Appendix K examines verbalized versus independent sampling, initial-seed versus refinement-dependent success, removal of the inner quality loop, and disagreement across 1,271 ensemble evaluations. Appendix H.2 adds missed-harm analysis. These substantially extend the retained transfer, reproducibility, false-positive, and vulnerability analyses.

E5.justification: Table 13 newly reports scores with ± quantities, although their statistical meaning is unspecified. Appendix K.5 adds inter-judge score standard deviations. Existing three-run transfer testing, five-run reproducibility testing, and human agreement reporting are retained; no increase in those repeat counts is established.

E6.justification: Existing Haiku, high-severity Opus 4.5, transfer, and reproducibility results are retained. New Table 1 entries report Operator success of 81.6%/67.8% and random-seed Opus 4.5 success of 85.0%/86.7% for OS/Multi-Apps; Section 5.2 reverses the latter domain percentages. Opus 4.6, baseline, ablation, and negative-audit results are also added. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The conceptual definitions and formal transfer-success formulation are retained. v2 adds empirical metrics and analyses, but no new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the conceptual framework, automatic elicitation from benign inputs, transferable vulnerabilities, and systematic analysis. Naming Operator in the abstract adds an example supporting the existing broad claim. Resources foregrounded in the revised introduction were already listed in v1's concluding experimental summary.

C2.justification: Appendix K adds substantive interpretations connecting diversity to verbalized sampling, elicitation to refinement, perturbation quality to the inner loop, and ensemble robustness to judge disagreement. Appendix H.2 adds claims about rarely missed harms, acknowledges oversensitivity to low-severity behavior, and proposes threshold adjustment. Earlier vulnerability interpretations and future-work discussion remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents baseline adaptations and execution schedules, additional summarizer settings, and detailed API costs and iteration counts for the new Operator and Opus evaluations. It also supplies negative-annotation guidelines and ablation configurations. Existing prompt templates, AWS configuration, and resource references are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for off-task actions, diversity measurement, and newly evaluated models, and explains why TAI3 is the closest adaptable baseline. The broader research positioning remains unchanged; several other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains separate high-severity and ablation subsections; Appendices F and H are reorganized around the expanded evaluations. The conceptual and methodological prose remains largely unchanged. Other edits include localized wording, cross-references, and replacement of the preprint footer with conference information.

P2.justification: Table 1 is restructured, with the original high-severity Opus results redistributed into summary and detailed Tables 2 and 8. New displays cover sampled-seed severity, baseline performance and quality, diversity, refinement dependence, and quality-loop ablation. Human-annotation tables move, while both original figures and the vulnerability tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Random-seed Opus testing and component ablations address selection and component-validation gaps in v1, while the negative-trajectory audit adds useful evaluator scrutiny. However, Appendix K.1 compares success per multi-attempt seed against success per individual mutation, and Table 12's severity percentages are inconsistently normalized. Appendix H.2 also interprets accuracy among predicted negatives as TNR and evidence of recall. These problems limit the added evidence's reliability, leaving a modest net improvement.
